### `photo_frame`

**Frame V automatically.** Frames V in photo mode without hand-tuned values: turns V to face the camera (plus yaw_offset degrees for a light sweep), puts the target (eyes: Both eyes and brows, filling the eyes region (the window's centre band).; face: The face from chin to hairline, filling the face region.; head-and-shoulders: Head and shoulders.; full-body: V from head to feet, standing.) at the centre of the window (or at position) and sets the field of view so span_m metres fill the window height. Each frame starts from its lens's known pose (face and eyes: a portrait lens from about 2 m, so repeated frames never drift) and stays within the lens's limits, or is refused. Any refusal or failure part-way puts back everything it changed whose earlier value the game reported (the field of view, V's placement, and the camera preset, roll and look-at it set), names anything it couldn't, and carries the undo in its detail. It measures where V is through the game's camera (or, if that isn't available, from window captures, more roughly) and corrects in a few steps; converged also needs V to face the requested direction within 3 degrees (residual.facing_deg). The result records the lens, the camera's distance, the chosen values and an undo.

- **Command:** `photo.frame`, run by the tools (it may call the bridge several times)
- **Permission:** Control photo mode (`write-photo`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** the result's undo puts the field of view, V's rotation and placement (and look-at, roll and camera preset) back as they were.
- **Refusals:** [`not_in_photo_mode`](#refusal-not-in-photo-mode), `framing_bound`, `no_projection`, `no_response`, `no_capture`, `not_found`, [`unavailable`](#refusal-unavailable), [`write_mismatch`](#refusal-write-mismatch)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `target` | string | `eyes`, `face`, `head-and-shoulders`, `full-body` | What to frame. Default face. |
| `span_m` | number | 0.02 to 5 | World height in metres that fills the window height (default: 0.2 eyes, 0.36 face, 0.8 head-and-shoulders, 2 full-body). |
| `offset` | object | the fields below | The target point relative to V's head joint, in metres (overrides the framing's own). |
| `offset.up` | number | -2 to 2 | Metres up. |
| `offset.forward` | number | -2 to 2 | Metres forward (V's facing). |
| `offset.right` | number | -2 to 2 | Metres to V's right. |
| `position` | object | the fields below | Where the target should sit, as fractions of the window (default the centre). |
| `position.x` | number | 0 to 1 | 0 left edge, 1 right edge. |
| `position.y` | number | 0 to 1 | 0 top edge, 1 bottom edge. |
| `xf_preset` | boolean | `true`, `false` | First select the framing's XF camera preset (6 full body, 7 face, 8 eyes, 9 head and shoulders; needs the test profile's preset file), then fine-tune. |
| `camera_preset` | integer | 0 to 9 | First select this photo-mode camera preset (0-9), then fine-tune. |
| `keep_roll` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Keep the camera preset's own roll. Default false: the camera is levelled (roll 0) after selecting a preset. |
| `reseat_camera` | boolean | `true`, `false` | 0.7: when photo mode's camera is more than 4 m from V (a drone camera flown off) and the lens isn't keep, first select camera preset 1 to bring it back near V. Default true. |
| `face_camera` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Turn V to face the camera first. Default true. |
| `yaw_offset` | number | -180 to 180 | Degrees V turns away from facing the camera (counter-clockwise seen from above), for light sweeps and profile checks: 90 shows V's right side, 180 the back of V's head. Photo Mode Ex keeps V's rotation within -180 to 180. |
| `lens` | string | `portrait`, `wide`, `keep` | Where the frame starts and the limits it keeps: portrait: A long lens from about 2 m: natural facial proportions (the default for face and eyes).; wide: A wide lens from about 30 cm (the old face framing): exaggerated perspective, for comparison.; keep: Start from the current camera and placement (the default for head-and-shoulders, full-body and after a camera preset).. Default: portrait for face and eyes, keep for the others and after a camera preset. A frame that would need to leave its lens's limits is refused (framing_bound) with the camera put back. |
| `look_at` | string | `keep`, `off`, `camera` | V's look-at before framing: keep (default), off (V's head follows the body, for light sweeps) or camera. |
| `method` | string | `auto`, `project`, `capture` | auto (default: the game's camera, else window captures), project (the game's camera only) or capture (window captures only). |
| `max_steps` | integer | 1 to 12 | Most correction steps (default 6). |
| `tolerance` | number | 0.001 to 0.2 | Allowed centring error as a fraction of the window height (default 0.01). |

### `photo_scene_set`

**Set photo mode's scene rows.** Photo mode's own scene rows, through its menu like every other setting: npcs (the surrounding NPCs row), weather (its weather row) and game_speed (0 to 1). npcs and weather each take {value} (the option's value from photo_state with options) or {label} (its on-screen text, matched loosely). Photo mode only; gone when photo mode closes. The answer carries the undo (the rows' earlier values).

- **Command:** `photo.scene.set`, the bridge method `photo.scene.set`
- **Permission:** Control photo mode (`write-photo`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** The result's undo sets the rows back; closing photo mode drops them too.
- **Refusals:** [`not_in_photo_mode`](#refusal-not-in-photo-mode), [`unavailable`](#refusal-unavailable), [`write_mismatch`](#refusal-write-mismatch)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `npcs` | object | the fields below | The surrounding NPCs row: {value} or {label}. |
| `npcs.value` | number | -1000 to 1000 | The option's value (photo_state's data). |
| `npcs.label` | string | 1 to 64 characters | The option's label. |
| `weather` | object | the fields below | The weather row: {value} or {label}. |
| `weather.value` | number | -1000 to 1000 | The option's value (photo_state's data). |
| `weather.label` | string | 1 to 64 characters | The option's label. |
| `game_speed` | number | 0 to 1 | The game-speed row, 0 to 1. |

## Appearance screen (character creator)

Read V's creator options, open the appearance screen from normal play, change options through their own rows, and confirm or back out.

### `player_appearance`

**V's appearance settings.** Reads V's character-creator state: body and voice, life path and hair-length tags. While the appearance screen (a mirror) is open it also lists every option with its current value; give option to see one option's full list of values. Outside the screen the game's option list isn't live, so only those flags are: the answer adds last_creator_reading, the last full list read on the screen this game session with its age in seconds (not live: a Back after it discarded its changes), when there is one. check asks whether V's finalized look has particular options (group and option names).

- **Command:** `player.appearance`, the bridge method `player.appearance`
- **Permission:** Look (`read`)
- **Changes the game:** No
- **Undo:** nothing to undo
- **Refusals:** [`game_not_ready`](#refusal-game-not-ready)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `option` | string | at most 128 characters | One option's internal name or on-screen label (appearance screen only). |
| `check` | array of object | at most 16 items | Options to look for in V's finalized look. |
| `check[].group` (required) | string | at most 128 characters | Customization group name. |
| `check[].option` (required) | string | at most 128 characters | Option name. |
| `check[].fpp` | boolean | `true`, `false` | First-person variant. |

### `cc_open`

**Open the appearance screen.** Opens the appearance screen (the mirror's character creator) from normal play, the way a mirror does, and waits until it is open. mode mirror (the default) allows the rows a mirror allows (hair, make-up, eye colour, piercings and the XF rows); ripperdoc also allows the face-shape, skin and cyberware rows. edit_mode new_game opens it in the new-game edit mode instead, as Character Customization Anywhere's F12 did in session 4: every row can change, the world isn't frozen, and Confirm still keeps the look; which edit mode avoids the stuck, half-open creator is a session 5 question. If the wait runs out, the request is withdrawn and the pause menu may open instead (Esc closes it). Refused in combat, a scene, a vehicle or a menu, when the player isn't V (a Johnny section), and until the game has registered the bridge's own save lock (it locks saving itself, until a save is loaded). If the wait runs out after the game took the request, the answer says the screen may still open (check game_status). Only in the XF test profile.

- **Command:** `cc.open`, the bridge method `cc.open`
- **Permission:** Change V's appearance (`write-character`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** cc.back (or Back in the appearance screen) discards every change made there and closes it.
- **Refusals:** [`creator_leave_disabled`](#refusal-creator-leave-disabled), [`not_in_gameplay`](#refusal-not-in-gameplay), [`not_safe_now`](#refusal-not-safe-now), [`not_v`](#refusal-not-v), [`save_lock_not_held`](#refusal-save-lock-not-held), [`creator_open_timeout`](#refusal-creator-open-timeout), [`creator_open_uncertain`](#refusal-creator-open-uncertain), [`unavailable`](#refusal-unavailable)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | string | `mirror`, `ripperdoc` | Which rows can be changed: mirror (default) or ripperdoc (adds the eye shape, nose, skin and cyberware rows). |
| `edit_mode` | string | `edit_tag`, `new_game` | The creator's edit mode: edit_tag (default: the mode's own tag, HairDresser or Ripperdoc, which freezes the world while the screen is open) or new_game (the NewGame tag Character Customization Anywhere's F12 ran with in session 4: every row editable, no freeze; not with mode ripperdoc). |
| `timeout_ms` | integer | 500 to 15000 | How long to wait for the screen, in milliseconds (default 5000). |

### `cc_apply`

**Change one appearance option.** While the appearance screen is open (at a mirror or ripperdoc), sets one character-creator option to a value, exactly as clicking it does. option is the option's internal name, its on-screen label (for example XF) or its slot (for example piercings_color or makeupLips_color, the colour row of whichever style is chosen: a colour row named by its own name, such as makeupLips_08, belongs to one style and is refused unless that style is chosen). Give index (counting from 0), value (a value's internal name or on-screen label, where 5 and 05 are the same position; a word such as gold also finds the one value whose name contains it) or label (the name the creator shows, matched loosely: case, spaces and punctuation don't matter, and every word given must appear, so Grace Bob V4 finds Grace - Side Swept Bob - V4); the answer gives the index chosen. It never confirms: the player keeps the look by confirming, or backs out to discard every change. Refused anywhere else.

- **Command:** `cc.apply`, run by the tools (it may call the bridge several times)
- **Permission:** Change V's appearance (`write-character`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** cc.apply with the previous index (in the result's undo), or Back in the appearance screen, which discards every change made there.
- **Refusals:** [`not_in_character_menu`](#refusal-not-in-character-menu), [`stale_match`](#refusal-stale-match), [`busy`](#refusal-busy)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `option` (required) | string | at most 128 characters | The option's internal name, on-screen label or slot. |
| `index` | integer | 0 to 100000 | The value, counting from 0. |
| `value` | string | at most 128 characters | The value's internal name or on-screen label, instead of index. |
| `label` | string | 1 to 128 characters | The value's name as the creator shows it, matched loosely (see above), instead of index. |
| `expect_option` | string | 1 to 128 characters | With index: the option row read before (player_appearance's option name); refused (stale_match) if option now resolves to another row. label does this itself. |
| `expect_value` | string | 1 to 256 characters | With index: the value's internal name read before at that index; refused (stale_match) if it has another name now. label does this itself. |

### `cc_page`

**Point the appearance screen's camera.** Moves the open appearance screen's camera to one part of V, as hovering over a row does: skin, hair, eyes, teeth, nose, lips, jaw, head, nails, body, or default (where the screen started). Changing an option through cc_apply already moves it to that option's part; this is for looking without changing anything.

- **Command:** `cc.page`, the bridge method `cc.page`
- **Permission:** Change V's appearance (`write-character`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** cc.page with page default (the camera's earlier part can't be read).
- **Refusals:** [`not_in_character_menu`](#refusal-not-in-character-menu)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `page` (required) | string | `skin`, `hair`, `eyes`, `teeth`, `nose`, `lips`, `jaw`, `head`, `nails`, `body`, `default` | The part of V to look at. |

### `cc_confirm`

**Confirm the appearance screen.** Presses Confirm on the open appearance screen (mirror or ripperdoc), keeping the look in the running game and closing the screen. Only in the XF test profile, and only in sessions that end by loading the safety save; saving stays locked while the change is live. Refused on a creator opened in new-game mode, where Confirm wouldn't keep the look.

- **Command:** `cc.confirm`, the bridge method `cc.confirm`
- **Permission:** Change V's appearance (`write-character`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** Load the safety save (the look stays in the running game until then).
- **Refusals:** [`creator_leave_disabled`](#refusal-creator-leave-disabled), [`not_in_character_menu`](#refusal-not-in-character-menu), [`busy`](#refusal-busy)

No parameters.

### `cc_back`

**Leave the appearance screen without keeping changes.** Presses Back on the open appearance screen and confirms it, discarding every change made there and closing the screen. It works even while the screen still seems busy with a change (a completion that never came): Back discards that change too, and the answer says busy_cleared. Only in the XF test profile.

- **Command:** `cc.back`, the bridge method `cc.back`
- **Permission:** Change V's appearance (`write-character`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** Nothing to undo: the changes made on the screen were discarded.
- **Refusals:** [`creator_leave_disabled`](#refusal-creator-leave-disabled), [`not_in_character_menu`](#refusal-not-in-character-menu)

No parameters.

## Player

Read V's state, move and turn her, turn her view, crouch, draw or holster, open menus, and give her back.

### `player_state`

**Read V's state.** V in the world: position (her feet: the entity's origin on the ground; 0.8.4, session 11's L5), facing (yaw), the camera's place (camera.position: in first person her eyes, about 1.6 m above position), direction, yaw and pitch, the player state machine (locomotion, high level, scene tier, vehicle, combat), whether she is in combat, a vehicle, a scene or a dialogue, why the bridge wouldn't move her now (busy), what she is looking at (with whether it is an interaction target), the effects the bridge put on her and the behaviours running.

- **Command:** `player.state`, the bridge method `player.state`
- **Permission:** Look (`read`)
- **Changes the game:** No
- **Undo:** nothing to undo
- **Refusals:** [`not_in_gameplay`](#refusal-not-in-gameplay)

No parameters.

### `player_teleport`

**Teleport V.** Moves V to a world point (position) or an offset from her (forward, right, up along her facing), and/or turns her (yaw absolute, turn relative), through the game's own teleport. By default the point snaps to walkable ground within 2 m and is refused where there is none (no_ground); ground exact skips the snap at your own risk. Either way a point more than 0.5 m away is refused where the world isn't loaded (not_streamed). At most 50 m unless far; at most two teleports a second. The answer reads her place back two ticks later (held). Positions here (position, before, now and the undo's) are her feet, as player_state's position, never the camera's: an undo with ground exact puts her feet back exactly where they were. It checks V first and refuses with the reason (in_combat, in_vehicle, in_scene, player_busy while she jumps, slides, falls or lands, swims, sits in a workspot, takes someone down or carries a body, or a menu or photo mode is open; player_state's busy_state says which).

- **Command:** `player.teleport`, the bridge method `player.teleport`
- **Permission:** Move V (`write-player`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** The result's undo teleports V back to where she stood, facing the same way; loading the save undoes it too.
- **Refusals:** [`not_in_gameplay`](#refusal-not-in-gameplay), [`not_v`](#refusal-not-v), [`in_combat`](#refusal-in-combat), [`in_vehicle`](#refusal-in-vehicle), [`in_scene`](#refusal-in-scene), [`player_busy`](#refusal-player-busy), [`no_ground`](#refusal-no-ground), [`not_streamed`](#refusal-not-streamed), [`too_far`](#refusal-too-far)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `position` | array of number | exactly 3 items | The world point [x, y, z]. |
| `offset` | object | the fields below | Where to, from V (instead of position). |
| `offset.forward` | number | -50 to 50 | Metres ahead of V. |
| `offset.right` | number | -50 to 50 | Metres to V's right. |
| `offset.up` | number | -10 to 10 | Metres up. |
| `yaw` | number | -360 to 360 | Face this yaw, degrees (0 along the world's +Y, counter-clockwise). |
| `turn` | number | -360 to 360 | Turn by this many degrees (left positive). |
| `ground` | string | `snap`, `exact` | snap (default: walkable ground within 2 m) or exact (no snap; the world must still be loaded there). |
| `far` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Allow more than 50 m (the destination must be loaded). |

### `player_look`

**Turn V's view.** Turns V's view to yaw and pitch (degrees; relative adds them to the current view) or towards a world point (at): instant (her facing by a teleport in place, the pitch by a very short look-at) or smooth over duration_s (along the shortest arc, eased in and out, in short steps of the game's own look-at, so it takes duration_s; the player's mouse or stick ends it, took_over camera_drift). Answers the angles reached, whether they are within 2 degrees, took_s and whether player_stop stopped it. Normal play only. It checks V first and refuses with the reason (in_combat, in_vehicle, in_scene, player_busy while she jumps, slides, falls or lands, swims, sits in a workspot, takes someone down or carries a body, or a menu or photo mode is open; player_state's busy_state says which).

- **Command:** `player.look`, the bridge method `player.look`
- **Permission:** Move V (`write-player`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** The result's undo turns the view back to the earlier angles.
- **Refusals:** [`not_in_gameplay`](#refusal-not-in-gameplay), [`not_v`](#refusal-not-v), [`in_combat`](#refusal-in-combat), [`in_vehicle`](#refusal-in-vehicle), [`in_scene`](#refusal-in-scene), [`player_busy`](#refusal-player-busy), [`unavailable`](#refusal-unavailable)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `yaw` | number | -360 to 360 | Yaw, degrees (0 along the world's +Y, counter-clockwise). |
| `pitch` | number | -170 to 170 | Pitch, degrees (up positive; -85 to 85 unless relative). |
| `relative` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Add yaw and pitch to the current view (default false). |
| `at` | array of number | exactly 3 items | Look at this world point [x, y, z] instead. |
| `mode` | string | `instant`, `smooth` | instant (default) or smooth. |
| `duration_s` | number | 0.05 to 5 | A smooth look's time, 0.05 to 5 s. Default 1. |

### `player_look_stop`

**End a look.** Ends a look the bridge started (smooth or behave_look), where the view is now.

- **Command:** `player.look.stop`, the bridge method `player.look.stop`
- **Permission:** Move V (`write-player`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** Nothing to undo.
- **Refusals:** [`not_in_gameplay`](#refusal-not-in-gameplay)

No parameters.

### `player_stop`

**Stop everything the bridge does with V.** Stops every behaviour, ends any look and lifts every effect the bridge put on V (a crouch, a glide's movement hold). Always allowed, like the kill switch, which does the same.

- **Command:** `player.stop`, the bridge method `player.stop`
- **Permission:** Stop the bridge (`control`)
- **Changes the game:** Only the bridge's own work: it stops or pauses it
- **Undo:** Start what you need again.

No parameters.

### `player_interact_list`

**List what V can interact with.** What the HUD offers now: the world interaction prompt (its title and choices, each with its index, label, input action and whether it is held) and any dialogue choices, plus which hub is active and which line is selected. Selecting a choice needs an input channel (research).

- **Command:** `player.interact.list`, the bridge method `player.interact.list`
- **Permission:** Look (`read`)
- **Changes the game:** No
- **Undo:** nothing to undo
- **Refusals:** [`not_in_gameplay`](#refusal-not-in-gameplay)

No parameters.

### `player_action`

**Do a system-driven action.** One of the actions the game's systems can do without input: crouch and stand (the game's own forced crouch, as a sniper nest uses it; only the bridge's own is lifted), weapon.draw, weapon.arms (0.7: the arm cyberware's weapon, such as Mantis Blades, drawn), weapon.holster and weapon.slot (1-3) through the equipment system's own requests, menu.open (inventory, map, journal, perks, crafting, or the wardrobe screen) and menu.close. Jumping, sprinting and dodging need an input channel (research). It checks V first and refuses with the reason (in_combat, in_vehicle, in_scene, player_busy while she jumps, slides, falls or lands, swims, sits in a workspot, takes someone down or carries a body, or a menu or photo mode is open; player_state's busy_state says which).

- **Command:** `player.action`, the bridge method `player.action`
- **Permission:** Move V (`write-player`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** The result's undo does the opposite (stand, weapon.holster, menu.close); player_stop and the kill switch lift a crouch too.
- **Refusals:** [`not_in_gameplay`](#refusal-not-in-gameplay), [`not_v`](#refusal-not-v), [`in_combat`](#refusal-in-combat), [`in_vehicle`](#refusal-in-vehicle), [`in_scene`](#refusal-in-scene), [`player_busy`](#refusal-player-busy), [`rate_limited`](#refusal-rate-limited)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` (required) | string | `crouch`, `stand`, `weapon.draw`, `weapon.arms`, `weapon.holster`, `weapon.slot`, `menu.open`, `menu.close` | The action. |
| `slot` | integer | 1 to 3 | With weapon.slot: the weapon slot 1-3. |
| `menu` | string | `inventory`, `map`, `journal`, `perks`, `crafting`, `wardrobe` | With menu.open: which menu. |

### `player_status`

**Read V's status.** V's life state in one read: health (points, maximum, percent), level and street cred with their experience, money (eddies), the wanted level (the police system's heat stage, the star state and whether the police chase V, beside the two quest facts for comparison), the vehicle V is in (mounted or not, which record, driver or passenger), an inventory summary (counts and quantities by item type, not a list; at most 1500 stacks are read, and total_stacks and truncated say when more were left), and the scanner (whether V is in scanner mode, how far the scan is, and what the scanner is on). parts picks some of vitals, progress, money, heat, vehicle, inventory and scanner (default all). Read only; player_state has V's position and movement. With no world to read it is refused game_loading (the bridge's gate, on the main menu, between sessions and during a load) or, if the gate is open but the game has no world yet, game_not_ready.

- **Command:** `player.status`, the bridge method `player.status`
- **Permission:** Look (`read`)
- **Changes the game:** No
- **Undo:** nothing to undo
- **Refusals:** [`game_not_ready`](#refusal-game-not-ready), [`not_in_gameplay`](#refusal-not-in-gameplay), [`game_loading`](#refusal-game-loading)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `parts` | array of string | at most 7 items; each `vitals`, `progress`, `money`, `heat`, `vehicle`, `inventory`, `scanner` | Which parts (default all): vitals, progress, money, heat, vehicle, inventory, scanner. |

## Behaviours

Routines that run inside the game at frame rate: a turntable, a smooth look, a glide along a walkable path, keeping a subject framed. Each streams its progress to the session's events and stops on `behave_stop`, the kill switch or loading a save.

### `behave_turntable`

**Turn showroom heads or rigs continuously.** A behaviour: the showroom's heads (or their light rigs, or both) turn continuously at deg_per_s, in the game at frame rate, until revolutions are done, max_s passes or behave_stop; then they turn back where they were unless return is false. Its progress and its end are in session_events.

- **Command:** `behave.turntable`, the bridge method `behave.turntable`
- **Permission:** Set up the finish showroom (`write-showroom`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** behave_stop with its id (the heads turn back); the kill switch and loading a save stop it too.
- **Refusals:** [`behaviour_limit`](#refusal-behaviour-limit), `no_showroom`, [`no_such_piece`](#refusal-no-such-piece)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `target` | string | `pieces`, `rigs`, `both` | pieces (default), rigs or both. |
| `pieces` | array of integer | at most 24 items; each 0 to 23 | Which heads by lineup index (default all). |
| `deg_per_s` | number | -360 to 360 | Degrees a second, -360 to 360 (positive turns them to their left). Default 30. |
| `revolutions` | number | 0.01 to 100 | Stop after this many turns, 0.01 to 100. |
| `return` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Turn them back where they were at the end (default true). |
| `max_s` | number | 0.1 to 600 | Stop after this many seconds, 0.1 to 600. Default 60 (a look: its duration plus 5 s; a glide: at most 30). |
| `every_ticks` | integer | 1 to 60 | Act every this many game ticks, 1 to 60 (default 2 for a turntable, 3 for keep_framed, else 1). |

### `behave_look`

**Turn V's view over time.** A behaviour: V's view turns towards a point (at) or to yaw and pitch (absolute degrees; turn for relative) over duration_s through the game's own look-at, watched each tick until it is within tolerance_deg (reached) or runs out (not_reached: the player's own mouse or stick breaks a look, as it breaks the game's). Normal play only.

- **Command:** `behave.look`, the bridge method `behave.look`
- **Permission:** Move V (`write-player`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** behave_stop ends it; player_look back to the earlier angles (in player_state) turns the view back.
- **Refusals:** [`behaviour_limit`](#refusal-behaviour-limit), [`not_in_gameplay`](#refusal-not-in-gameplay), [`not_v`](#refusal-not-v), [`in_combat`](#refusal-in-combat), [`in_vehicle`](#refusal-in-vehicle), [`in_scene`](#refusal-in-scene), [`player_busy`](#refusal-player-busy), [`user_took_over`](#refusal-user-took-over)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `at` | array of number | exactly 3 items | A world point to look at [x, y, z]. |
| `yaw` | number | -360 to 360 | The view's yaw, degrees (0 along the world's +Y, counter-clockwise). |
| `pitch` | number | -85 to 85 | The view's pitch, degrees (up positive), -85 to 85. |
| `turn` | object | the fields below | A relative turn instead of absolute angles. |
| `turn.yaw` | number | -360 to 360 | Turn by this yaw, degrees. |
| `turn.pitch` | number | -170 to 170 | Tilt by this pitch, degrees. |
| `duration_s` | number | 0.05 to 5 | How long the turn takes, 0.05 to 5 s. Default 1. |
| `tolerance_deg` | number | 0.2 to 10 | Close enough, 0.2 to 10 degrees. Default 2. |
| `max_s` | number | 0.1 to 600 | Stop after this many seconds, 0.1 to 600. Default 60 (a look: its duration plus 5 s; a glide: at most 30). |
| `every_ticks` | integer | 1 to 60 | Act every this many game ticks, 1 to 60 (default 2 for a turntable, 3 for keep_framed, else 1). |

### `behave_glide_path`

**Glide V along a walkable path.** A behaviour: V moves along the game's own walkable path (navmesh) to a point (to) or an offset from her (forward, right), at speed_m_s, by a teleport every tick, with her own movement held off meanwhile. V is checked every tick: it stops when she arrives, when the player's own input moves her (user_took_over: movement, jump, crouch, sprint, dodge or camera), when she is no longer free to move (combat, a vehicle, a scene, a fall or landing, swimming, a workspot, a takedown, a carried body), at max_s (at most 30 s) or on behave_stop, and gives her movement back. No walk animation plays (animated: false). At most 50 m of path. Normal play only.

- **Command:** `behave.glide.path`, the bridge method `behave.glide.path`
- **Permission:** Move V (`write-player`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** behave_stop ends it; its stop event carries a player_teleport undo back to the start.
- **Refusals:** [`behaviour_limit`](#refusal-behaviour-limit), [`not_in_gameplay`](#refusal-not-in-gameplay), [`not_v`](#refusal-not-v), [`in_combat`](#refusal-in-combat), [`in_vehicle`](#refusal-in-vehicle), [`in_scene`](#refusal-in-scene), [`player_busy`](#refusal-player-busy), [`user_took_over`](#refusal-user-took-over), [`no_path`](#refusal-no-path), [`no_ground`](#refusal-no-ground), [`not_streamed`](#refusal-not-streamed), [`too_far`](#refusal-too-far), [`bridge_effects_active`](#refusal-bridge-effects-active)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `to` | array of number | exactly 3 items | The world point to glide to [x, y, z]. |
| `offset` | object | the fields below | Where to go, from V (instead of to). |
| `offset.forward` | number | -50 to 50 | Metres ahead of V. |
| `offset.right` | number | -50 to 50 | Metres to V's right. |
| `speed_m_s` | number | 0.2 to 6 | Speed, 0.2 to 6 m/s. Default 1.4 (a walk). |
| `max_s` | number | 0.1 to 600 | Stop after this many seconds, 0.1 to 600. Default 60 (a look: its duration plus 5 s; a glide: at most 30). |
| `every_ticks` | integer | 1 to 60 | Act every this many game ticks, 1 to 60 (default 2 for a turntable, 3 for keep_framed, else 1). |

### `behave_keep_framed`

**Keep a subject framed as the camera moves.** A behaviour: keeps a subject at a frame position (at, window heights from the centre; default the centre) while the camera moves. subject piece: a showroom head is moved onto the camera's view ray at distance_m (default its distance at the start), facing the camera, exactly from the camera's pose (needs the showroom permission too). subject v: in photo mode, V's placement (left/right, up/down) is steered from a measured response, as photo_frame measures it, refined after each step. Stops at max_s or on behave_stop; its stop event carries the undo.

- **Command:** `behave.keep.framed`, the bridge method `behave.keep.framed`
- **Permission:** Control photo mode (`write-photo`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** behave_stop ends it; the stop event's undo puts V's placement back (a head stays where it was last put; showroom_spawn resets the lineup).
- **Refusals:** [`behaviour_limit`](#refusal-behaviour-limit), [`not_in_photo_mode`](#refusal-not-in-photo-mode), [`no_such_piece`](#refusal-no-such-piece), [`unavailable`](#refusal-unavailable)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `subject` | string | `piece`, `v` | piece (a showroom head, default) or v (V in photo mode). |
| `piece` | integer | 0 to 23 | The showroom head's index, with subject piece. |
| `at` | object | the fields below | Where in the frame (default the centre). |
| `at.x` | number | -1.2 to 1.2 | Across, window heights from the centre (right positive). |
| `at.y` | number | -0.5 to 0.5 | Down, window heights from the centre. |
| `distance_m` | number | 0.3 to 20 | A head's eyes this far from the camera, 0.3 to 20 m (default: as at the start). |
| `tolerance` | number | 0.002 to 0.2 | Close enough, 0.002 to 0.2 window heights. Default 0.02. |
| `max_step` | number | 0.01 to 0.5 | V's largest placement step, 0.01 to 0.5. Default 0.1. |
| `piece_eyes` | array of number | exactly 3 items | A showroom head's eyes in its own frame (default the showroom build's). |
| `max_s` | number | 0.1 to 600 | Stop after this many seconds, 0.1 to 600. Default 60 (a look: its duration plus 5 s; a glide: at most 30). |
| `every_ticks` | integer | 1 to 60 | Act every this many game ticks, 1 to 60 (default 2 for a turntable, 3 for keep_framed, else 1). |

### `behave_stop`

**Stop behaviours.** Stops one behaviour (id) or all of them. Each stops on the next game tick and gives back what it held (a turntable turns its heads back, a glide gives V her movement back); session_events says how each ended.

- **Command:** `behave.stop`, the bridge method `behave.stop`
- **Permission:** Stop the bridge (`control`)
- **Changes the game:** Only the bridge's own work: it stops or pauses it
- **Undo:** Start the behaviour again.
- **Refusals:** [`no_such_behaviour`](#refusal-no-such-behaviour)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | integer | at least 1 | The behaviour's id (from its start or behave_list). |
| `all` | boolean | `true`, `false` | true: stop every behaviour. |
| `reason` | string | at most 64 characters | Why, for the log. |

### `behave_list`

**List running behaviours.** The behaviours running in the game now: id, kind, target, state, how long they have run and a summary (how far a head has turned, a glide travelled, a look's remaining angle).

- **Command:** `behave.list`, the bridge method `behave.list`
- **Permission:** Look (`read`)
- **Changes the game:** No
- **Undo:** nothing to undo

No parameters.

## World

Read the world's state, probe the ground and streaming around V, and set the clock, the weather, a freeze or XF map pins.

### `world_time_set`

**Set the time of day.** Sets the in-game clock (hours, minutes, seconds) while V is in the world or the appearance screen is open (to compare the screen's light at different times of day without leaving it), or restores an exact earlier time with total_seconds. In photo mode it sets photo mode's own time of day instead (the Environment tab's slider, hours and minutes only; a photo-mode setting, so the photo write class must be allowed too). Whether the world's clock is as before once photo mode closes is not established yet (game_status's world_time_seconds shows it). target photo or world names the clock: a photo-mode undo carries target photo, so replayed after photo mode closes it changes nothing rather than the world's clock. Changing the world clock can trigger timed events in quests, so use a disposable save.

- **Command:** `world.time.set`, the bridge method `world.time.set`
- **Permission:** Change the world (`write-world`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** the result's undo: the world's clock with total_seconds (target world), or photo mode's time of day in hours and minutes (target photo), which changes nothing once photo mode has closed.
- **Refusals:** [`not_in_gameplay`](#refusal-not-in-gameplay), [`not_in_photo_mode`](#refusal-not-in-photo-mode), [`unavailable`](#refusal-unavailable)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hours` | integer | 0 to 23 | Hour, 0 to 23. |
| `minutes` | integer | 0 to 59 | Minute, 0 to 59. |
| `seconds` | integer | 0 to 59 | Second, 0 to 59. |
| `total_seconds` | integer | 0 to 2147483647 | An exact earlier time from a previous result's undo (the world's clock only). |
| `target` | string | `world`, `photo` | Which clock: world (refused in photo mode) or photo (photo mode's own time of day; outside photo mode nothing changes). Default: photo in photo mode, else world. |

### `world_pause`

**Freeze the world.** Freezes everything around V (paused: true), the way the appearance screen does, or unfreezes it (paused: false). Only in normal play: photo mode and the appearance screen already freeze the world.

- **Command:** `world.pause`, the bridge method `world.pause`
- **Permission:** Change the world (`write-world`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** world.pause with paused: false; the kill switch also unfreezes.
- **Refusals:** [`not_in_gameplay`](#refusal-not-in-gameplay), [`game_not_ready`](#refusal-game-not-ready)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `paused` (required) | boolean | `true`, `false` | true freezes, false unfreezes. |

### `world_pin`

**Place an XF map pin.** Temporary test feature (bridge 0.5.3). Places a map pin with an XF badge and a label, shown on the world map (with the label in its tooltip), on the minimap and in the world through walls, the way the game shows its own markers: the game's own pin icon, with the XF badge above it and the label on the pin's name line. Give exactly one of position [x, y, z] (a world point in metres, as game_status and showroom_state report them), piece (a showroom head's index: the pin's point is at its crown, 0.12 m above its eyes by default, and the game draws its marker just above that point; placed there, so turning the head leaves it and clearing the heads removes it) or at: "v" (above where V stands now). label names it (1-48 characters). variant picks the game's pin type whose map filter and icon it uses: custom (default; the one the minimap draws for any placed pin), interaction (in the world only), apartment, clothes or default. lift_m raises it (metres; default 0 at a position, 0.12 above a head's eyes, 0.45 above V). ui_state's pins[].xf_mark gives where the XF mark is (px, its top-left corner in window pixels) and where the pin's own point is (point_px). The answer's pins list which views have drawn each pin so far (drawn_by: world, minimap, world_map), and the plugin log names each one the first time. At most 8 pins. world.pin.clear, the kill switch and loading a save remove them.

- **Command:** `world.pin`, the bridge method `world.pin`
- **Permission:** Change the world (`write-world`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** world.pin.clear with the result's id; the kill switch and loading a save also remove every XF pin.
- **Refusals:** [`not_in_world`](#refusal-not-in-world), [`not_ready`](#refusal-not-ready), `too_many_pins`, [`no_such_piece`](#refusal-no-such-piece), [`not_spawned_yet`](#refusal-not-spawned-yet), `pin_refused`

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `position` | array of number | exactly 3 items | A world point [x, y, z] in metres. |
| `piece` | integer | 0 to 23 | A showroom head's index (0 to 23), from showroom_state. |
| `at` | string | `v` | v: above where V stands now. |
| `label` (required) | string | 1 to 400 characters | The pin's name, 1 to 48 characters (longer is cut). |
| `variant` | string | `custom`, `interaction`, `apartment`, `clothes`, `default` | The game's pin type it borrows its map filter and icon from. Default custom. |
| `lift_m` | number | -5 to 5 | Metres above the point (-5 to 5). |

### `world_pin_clear`

**Remove XF map pins.** Temporary test feature (bridge 0.5.3). Removes one XF map pin by the id world_pin answered, or every XF pin without an id.

- **Command:** `world.pin.clear`, the bridge method `world.pin.clear`
- **Permission:** Change the world (`write-world`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** world.pin places a pin again.
- **Refusals:** `no_such_pin`

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | integer | 1 to 1000000 | The pin's id from world_pin; leave out to remove all. |

### `world_state`

**Read the world's state.** The world as it is now: the clock (day, time, paused, time dilation, the bridge's freeze), the rain (type, intensity, puddles, moisture), the weather state's name and this world's weather states (with Codeware; without it only the rain is readable), named quest facts (facts: their values, read only), and in photo mode its own time, weather, NPC and game-speed rows with their options. Changes nothing.

- **Command:** `world.state`, the bridge method `world.state`
- **Permission:** Look (`read`)
- **Changes the game:** No
- **Undo:** nothing to undo
- **Refusals:** [`game_not_ready`](#refusal-game-not-ready)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `facts` | array of string | at most 16 items; each at most 96 characters; matches `^[A-Za-z0-9_.]+$` | Quest fact names to read (at most 16). |

### `world_probe`

**Probe the world at points.** Observe only: at each point (points, up to 16, or a ring around V with around_v), whether the walkable ground around it is loaded (streamed), the nearest walkable point within radius_m, the ground below (a static-geometry ray down_m down) and the ceiling above, and the distance from V. For choosing a place before a teleport, a glide or a showroom; nothing is moved or loaded.

- **Command:** `world.probe`, the bridge method `world.probe`
- **Permission:** Look (`read`)
- **Changes the game:** No
- **Undo:** nothing to undo
- **Refusals:** [`unavailable`](#refusal-unavailable)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `points` | array of array of number | 1 to 16 items; each exactly 3 items | World points to probe. |
| `around_v` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Probe V's place and a ring around her instead of points. |
| `ring_m` | number | 0.5 to 50 | The ring's radius, 0.5 to 50 m. Default 3. |
| `count` | integer | 1 to 15 | Points on the ring, 1 to 15. Default 8. |
| `radius_m` | number | 0.2 to 10 | How far to look for walkable ground from each point, 0.2 to 10 m. Default 2. |
| `down_m` | number | 0.5 to 100 | How far below each point the ground ray looks, 0.5 to 100 m. Default 10. |
| `clearance_m` | number | 0.05 to 3 | Also cast eight level rays this long from each point and report which are blocked (free space), 0.05 to 3 m. |
| `sight_from` | array of number | exactly 3 items | Also check the sight line from this world point to each point (static geometry between). |

### `world_weather_set`

**Set the weather.** Holds one of this world's weather states (name, as world_state lists them, blending over blend_s seconds), which stops the game's own weather cycle, or gives the weather back to the cycle (cycle: true, with or without a name). Needs Codeware (detected, never installed). Refused in a story scene (quest_scene), where the story may hold the weather; elsewhere a quest's own weather hold can still win, and giving the weather back to the cycle ends such a hold too (the answer's note says so). The answer carries the undo (the earlier state and the cycle back on); the kill switch does the same. A save made meanwhile would keep the weather, so the save lock stays on and game_save refuses until it is undone.

- **Command:** `world.weather.set`, the bridge method `world.weather.set`
- **Permission:** Change the world (`write-world`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** The result's undo sets the earlier weather and turns the game's cycle back on; the kill switch does the same.
- **Refusals:** [`codeware_missing`](#refusal-codeware-missing), [`quest_scene`](#refusal-quest-scene), [`not_in_gameplay`](#refusal-not-in-gameplay), [`call_failed`](#refusal-call-failed), [`unavailable`](#refusal-unavailable)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | at most 96 characters; matches `^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$` | The weather state, such as 24h_weather_rain. |
| `blend_s` | number | 0 to 60 | Blend time, 0 to 60 seconds. Default 2. |
| `cycle` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Give the weather back to the game's own cycle (after setting name, if given). |

### `world_facts`

**Read quest facts in a batch.** Reads many named quest facts in one call: facts (a list of at most 128 names) and/or preset. The preset main_story is the 93 main-story facts of the 2.31 quest data (research/story-engine/main-story-facts.json; the answer also groups them by category), final_boards the 29 the game's final boards read. Names are letters, digits, _ and . only. A fact the game never set reads 0, the same as one set to 0. Read only; world_state reads up to 16 facts beside the clock and weather. With no world to read it is refused game_loading (the bridge's gate, on the main menu, between sessions and during a load) or, if the gate is open but the game has no world yet, game_not_ready.

- **Command:** `world.facts`, the bridge method `world.facts`
- **Permission:** Look (`read`)
- **Changes the game:** No
- **Undo:** nothing to undo
- **Refusals:** [`game_not_ready`](#refusal-game-not-ready), [`unavailable`](#refusal-unavailable), [`game_loading`](#refusal-game-loading)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `facts` | array of string | at most 128 items; each at most 96 characters; matches `^[A-Za-z0-9_.]+$` | Quest fact names to read (at most 128). |
| `preset` | string | `main_story`, `final_boards` | A named list of facts, read with any extra facts: main_story (The main-story facts of the 2.31 quest data (93), grouped in the answer by category.) final_boards (The facts the game's own final boards read (29): whose fate matters for the ending.) |

### `world_district`

**Read V's district.** Where V is in Night City's own terms, from the game's district system (the one the minimap and the police use): the innermost area, and above it the subdistrict and district (a place such as Kabuki_NoTellMotel inside Kabuki inside Watson), each with its name, type, crime multiplier and gangs, the police preset in force, Dogtown and Badlands flags, and the map's own location text as a cross-check. District is not position: player_state has the coordinates. Refused with no_district for a moment after a load, until the game has told its district system where V is. Read only. With no world to read it is refused game_loading (the bridge's gate, on the main menu, between sessions and during a load) or, if the gate is open but the game has no world yet, game_not_ready.

- **Command:** `world.district`, the bridge method `world.district`
- **Permission:** Look (`read`)
- **Changes the game:** No
- **Undo:** nothing to undo
- **Refusals:** [`game_not_ready`](#refusal-game-not-ready), [`no_district`](#refusal-no-district), [`unavailable`](#refusal-unavailable), [`game_loading`](#refusal-game-loading)

No parameters.

## Wardrobe, clothing and cyberware

Read and change what V wears and her cyberware, through the game's own equipment requests. Off in every build until writes to V's inventory are approved.

### `inventory_equip`

**Equip a clothing item on V.** Equips a clothing item on V by its item record (for example Items.Helmet_01_basic_01), as the inventory screen does, and waits until the slot shows it. With add_if_missing, an item V doesn't have is added to V's inventory first (and remembered, so inventory_unequip can remove it again). Clothing slots only (Head, Face, OuterChest, InnerChest, Legs, Feet, Outfit); only in normal play, not in combat or a scene. When an active wardrobe outfit (or a hidden area) decides what the slot shows, the item is equipped but doesn't draw: the answer says so (hidden_by_outfit, outfit) and wardrobe_equip is the next step. Needs the inventory permission, which the bridge's settings keep off until the maintainer allows it.

- **Command:** `inventory.equip`, the bridge method `inventory.equip`
- **Permission:** Change V's clothing (`write-inventory`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** the result's undo equips the earlier item's exact copy again (its id), or empties the slot (removing an item the bridge added); loading a save also undoes it.
- **Refusals:** [`not_in_gameplay`](#refusal-not-in-gameplay), [`not_safe_now`](#refusal-not-safe-now), [`not_v`](#refusal-not-v), [`not_in_inventory`](#refusal-not-in-inventory), [`call_failed`](#refusal-call-failed), [`timeout`](#refusal-timeout)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `item` (required) | string | at most 128 characters; matches `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+(\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+)+$` | The item record, for example Items.Helmet_01_basic_01. |
| `slot` | string | `Head`, `Face`, `OuterChest`, `InnerChest`, `Legs`, `Feet`, `Outfit` | The clothing slot, checked against the item's own (optional). |
| `add_if_missing` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Add the item to V's inventory if V doesn't have it. Default false. |
| `id` | string | at most 20 characters; matches `^[0-9]{1,20}$` | The exact copy to equip, as an undo names it (the decimal identity the game gave); without it, any copy of the record. When V no longer has that copy, another copy is equipped and the answer says exact: false. |

### `inventory_list`

**List the clothing V owns.** Observe only: the clothing items in V's own inventory, one entry per copy: its item record (inventory_equip's item), clothing slot (Head, Face, OuterChest, InnerChest, Legs, Feet, Outfit), id (that exact copy's identity, inventory_equip's id), its name in the game's language and whether V wears it now; count says how many there are in all, listed how many the answer carries. slot lists one slot only. Nothing is changed, and the inventory permission isn't needed. Items stored only in the wardrobe aren't listed (wardrobe_state shows those).

- **Command:** `inventory.list`, the bridge method `inventory.list`
- **Permission:** Look (`read`)
- **Changes the game:** No
- **Undo:** nothing to undo
- **Refusals:** [`unavailable`](#refusal-unavailable), [`game_not_ready`](#refusal-game-not-ready)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `slot` | string | `Head`, `Face`, `OuterChest`, `InnerChest`, `Legs`, `Feet`, `Outfit` | Only this clothing slot. |
| `limit` | integer | 1 to 200 | At most this many entries, 1 to 200. Default 100. |

### `wardrobe_state`

**Read V's wardrobe outfit.** The wardrobe outfit V wears (set 1-7, or 0 for none) and, for each clothing area (Head, Face, OuterChest, InnerChest, Legs, Feet), what it shows: outfit (the outfit's item), hidden (nothing: the outfit leaves the area empty, or headgear is hidden), equipped or empty; plus what is equipped there and the wardrobe's stored outfits. An active outfit overrides what the equipment slots show, which is why an equipped helmet can stay invisible. manager says who decides: wardrobe (a wardrobe outfit, set 1-7), script (a script mod's outfit system, named in managed_by when known, such as EquipmentEx: active is true while set is 0, and the wardrobe's own requests don't reach it) or none (what is equipped shows); suspended_by_bridge says the bridge took an outfit off (wardrobe_equip resume puts it back); script_outfit is Equipment-EX's outfit when it is installed (its version, active and its parts: outfit slot, item and the item's exact identity; available false with why when the installed Equipment-EX lacks a function the bridge calls, and then only suspend and resume drive it).

- **Command:** `wardrobe.state`, the bridge method `wardrobe.state`
- **Permission:** Look (`read`)
- **Changes the game:** No
- **Undo:** nothing to undo
- **Refusals:** [`not_in_gameplay`](#refusal-not-in-gameplay), [`unavailable`](#refusal-unavailable)

No parameters.

### `wardrobe_equip`

**Change V's wardrobe outfit.** Changes what V's clothing shows through the wardrobe, as the wardrobe screen does (the equipment system's own requests; stored outfits are never edited or saved): set applies outfit 1-7; clear takes the outfit off, so V shows what is equipped; item shows that clothing item in its area of the active outfit (the item must be in V's inventory or the wardrobe); area with show equipped makes that area show what is equipped there, and show hidden hides it; restore (the undo) puts back exactly the outfit and each area a snapshot recorded (with no outfit too: each area's hidden state; the same copy of each item when V still has it, and everything it still can, naming what neither the wardrobe nor V's inventory has any more in not_restored); suspend takes the outfit off with the story's own request, whoever manages it (the wardrobe or a script mod's outfit system such as EquipmentEx), so equipped clothing draws, and resume puts that outfit back. Under a script mod's outfit system, item puts the item into that outfit where the bridge can drive it (Equipment-EX: its own outfit system, as its screen does; the undo restores its parts exactly), and suspend and resume work for any; the rest is refused (outfit_managed_elsewhere). Waits until the wardrobe shows the change. Only in normal play, not in combat or a scene. Needs the inventory permission; the kill switch puts back the wardrobe as it was before the bridge's first change.

- **Command:** `wardrobe.equip`, the bridge method `wardrobe.equip`
- **Permission:** Change V's clothing (`write-inventory`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** the result's undo (wardrobe_equip with restore, or resume after suspend) puts the outfit and every area back exactly; the kill switch resumes a suspended outfit and restores the wardrobe as it was before the bridge's first change.
- **Refusals:** [`not_in_gameplay`](#refusal-not-in-gameplay), [`not_safe_now`](#refusal-not-safe-now), [`not_v`](#refusal-not-v), [`not_in_inventory`](#refusal-not-in-inventory), [`call_failed`](#refusal-call-failed), [`no_active_outfit`](#refusal-no-active-outfit), [`outfit_managed_elsewhere`](#refusal-outfit-managed-elsewhere), [`script_outfit_api_changed`](#refusal-script-outfit-api-changed), [`timeout`](#refusal-timeout)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `set` | integer | 1 to 7 | Apply this wardrobe outfit (1-7; wardrobe_state lists the stored ones). |
| `clear` | boolean | `true`, `false` | true: take the active outfit off. |
| `item` | string | at most 128 characters; matches `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+(\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+)+$` | Show this clothing item record in its area of the active outfit, for example Items.Helmet_01_basic_01. |
| `area` | string | `Head`, `Face`, `OuterChest`, `InnerChest`, `Legs`, `Feet` | The clothing area for show. |
| `show` | string | `equipped`, `hidden` | With area: equipped (the area shows what is equipped there) or hidden (nothing). |
| `suspend` | boolean | `true`, `false` | true: take the outfit off for now with the story's own request (works under the wardrobe and script outfit systems alike), so equipped clothing draws; the undo is resume. |
| `resume` | boolean | `true`, `false` | true: put back the outfit the bridge took off with suspend. |
| `restore` | object | the fields below | A wardrobe_equip answer's undo: the outfit (0 none) and what each area showed. |
| `restore.set` (required) | integer | 0 to 7 | The outfit that was active, 0 for none. |
| `restore.slots` | array of object | at most 6 items | What each area showed. |
| `restore.slots[].area` (required) | string | `Head`, `Face`, `OuterChest`, `InnerChest`, `Legs`, `Feet` | The clothing area. |
| `restore.slots[].item` | string | at most 128 characters | The outfit's item in the area (empty: none). |
| `restore.slots[].id` | string | at most 20 characters; matches `^[0-9]{1,20}$` | The item's exact identity as the snapshot reported it (0.6.1: the same copy is put back when V still has it). |
| `restore.slots[].hidden` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Whether the area was hidden. |
| `restore.script_outfit` | object | the fields below | A script outfit system's outfit when the snapshot was taken (Equipment-EX): on or off, and its parts. |
| `restore.script_outfit.active` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Whether that outfit was on. |
| `restore.script_outfit.parts` | array of object | at most 64 items | Each outfit slot in use and its item. |
| `restore.script_outfit.parts[].slot` (required) | string | at most 128 characters | The outfit slot record, e.g. OutfitSlots.Head. |
| `restore.script_outfit.parts[].item` (required) | string | at most 128 characters | The item record. |
| `restore.script_outfit.parts[].id` | string | at most 20 characters; matches `^[0-9]{1,20}$` | The item's exact identity as the snapshot reported it (0.6.1). |

### `inventory_unequip`

**Take off a clothing item.** Takes off what V wears in one clothing slot (slot), or the given item (item), and waits until the slot is empty. remove_added also takes the item out of V's inventory, but only an item the bridge itself added this session. Needs the inventory permission.

- **Permission:** Change V's clothing (`write-inventory`)

- **Undo:** the result's undo equips the earlier item again.
- **Refusals:** [`not_in_gameplay`](#refusal-not-in-gameplay), [`not_safe_now`](#refusal-not-safe-now), [`not_v`](#refusal-not-v), [`not_in_inventory`](#refusal-not-in-inventory), [`call_failed`](#refusal-call-failed), [`not_added_by_bridge`](#refusal-not-added-by-bridge), [`timeout`](#refusal-timeout)

|---|---|---|---|
| `slot` | string | `Head`, `Face`, `OuterChest`, `InnerChest`, `Legs`, `Feet`, `Outfit` | The clothing slot to empty. |
| `item` | string | at most 128 characters; matches `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+(\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+)+$` | The item record to take off (instead of slot). |
| `remove_added` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Also remove the item from V's inventory if the bridge added it (with item). Default false. |

### `cyberware_state`

**Read V's cyberware.** What each of V's cyberware areas holds (ArmsCW, HandsCW, EyesCW, FaceCW, FrontalCortexCW, SystemReplacementCW, NervousSystemCW, CardiovascularSystemCW, ImmuneSystemCW, IntegumentarySystemCW, MusculoskeletalSystemCW, LegsCW), slot by slot with each item's record and name; for the arms, the chain the character creator's holster state follows (the ArmsCW item's holstered item and its appearance, such as holstered_mantis, and the creator group that draws it), what the right-arm and weapon slots hold now, drawn (the arm cyberware is out, by the rule cyberware changes are refused by), and whether a no-arm-cyberware effect is on; V's humanity. areas limits the list.

- **Command:** `cyberware.state`, the bridge method `cyberware.state`
- **Permission:** Look (`read`)
- **Changes the game:** No

### `cyberware_equip`

**Equip a cyberware item.** Puts a cyberware item into its area's slot through the game's own equipment request, as a ripperdoc's screen does (the earlier item in that slot comes out first): item is its record (Items.StrongArms, Items.MantisBlades, Items.NanoWires, Items.ProjectileLauncher, ...), slot the slot (default the first empty one), add_if_missing adds it to V's inventory first and remembers it. Only in normal play, outside combat and scenes; while the arm cyberware is drawn (after photo mode it stays drawn) the tools holster it first with the game's own request (holster_first: false refuses arms_drawn instead); the game's own equip requirements are checked before anything changes (not_equippable leaves nothing added). The answer reads the slot back and carries the undo (the exact earlier copy back, with a copy the bridge added removed, or the slot emptied and an added item removed); if the slot can't be read back, equipped is unknown and the undo is still given. V's look and stats change until the undo, the kill switch or a load; the save lock is held meanwhile and game_save refuses until it is undone. In the inventory class, off unless allowed.

- **Command:** `cyberware.equip`, run by the tools (it may call the bridge several times)
- **Permission:** Change V's clothing (`write-inventory`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** The result's undo puts the earlier item back, or empties the slot and removes an item the bridge added; loading the save undoes it too.
- **Refusals:** [`not_in_gameplay`](#refusal-not-in-gameplay), [`not_safe_now`](#refusal-not-safe-now), [`not_v`](#refusal-not-v), [`not_in_inventory`](#refusal-not-in-inventory), [`call_failed`](#refusal-call-failed), [`arms_drawn`](#refusal-arms-drawn), [`not_equippable`](#refusal-not-equippable), [`unavailable`](#refusal-unavailable)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `item` (required) | string | at most 128 characters; matches `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_.]+$` | The cyberware item's record, such as Items.MantisBlades. |
| `slot` | integer | 0 to 9 | The slot, 0 to 9 (default: the first empty one). |
| `add_if_missing` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Add the item to V's inventory first if V doesn't have it (removed again by the undo). |
| `id` | string | matches `^[0-9]{1,24}$` | The exact copy to equip, as an undo names it (digits). |
| `remove_added_item` | string | at most 128 characters; matches `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_.]+$` | After the equip, remove the copy of this record the bridge added (a swap's undo gives it). |
| `holster_first` | boolean | `true`, `false` | When V has her arm cyberware out, holster it first with the game's own request and then make the change (default true); false refuses arms_drawn instead. |

### `cyberware_unequip`

**Empty a cyberware slot.** Takes a cyberware item out of its slot through the game's own unequip request: area (ArmsCW, ...) and slot (one of the area's unlocked slots), or item (its record; its own slot is found). remove_added also removes an item the bridge itself added this session. - **Refusals:** [`not_in_gameplay`](#refusal-not-in-gameplay), [`not_safe_now`](#refusal-not-safe-now), [`not_v`](#refusal-not-v), [`not_in_inventory`](#refusal-not-in-inventory), [`call_failed`](#refusal-call-failed), [`arms_drawn`](#refusal-arms-drawn), [`not_added_by_bridge`](#refusal-not-added-by-bridge)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `area` | string | `ArmsCW`, `HandsCW`, `EyesCW`, `FaceCW`, `FrontalCortexCW`, `SystemReplacementCW`, `NervousSystemCW`, `CardiovascularSystemCW`, `ImmuneSystemCW`, `IntegumentarySystemCW`, `MusculoskeletalSystemCW`, `LegsCW` | The cyberware area. |

## XF Finish Showroom

Spawn, light, turn and clear the showroom's mannequin heads for close-up finish checks. Nothing is saved: clearing, the kill switch or loading a save removes them.

### `showroom_spawn`

**Set out the finish showroom.** Spawns XF Finish Showroom's mannequin heads, one per makeup preset of a showroom build (its folder or manifest.json from tools/build_showroom_package.ts), each on a black pedestal: in an arc about the camera (default; every head faces it) or a row across the view, spacing_m apart, each head's eyes distance_m from the camera (in photo mode) or V's eyes, as photo_frame's distance_m measures to V, and at height_m above V's ground (default: the camera's height with the camera as anchor, so the heads look straight into it; a head's natural height with V as anchor). Needs Codeware in the game and the showroom's archive staged. Nothing is saved: showroom.clear, the kill switch or loading a save removes them.

- **Command:** `showroom.spawn`, run by the tools (it may call the bridge several times)
- **Permission:** Set up the finish showroom (`write-showroom`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** showroom.clear with what: pieces (or all); loading a save also removes them.
- **Refusals:** [`codeware_missing`](#refusal-codeware-missing), [`showroom_missing`](#refusal-showroom-missing), `showroom_manifest_missing`, `showroom_manifest_bad`, `showroom_not_staged`, [`not_in_world`](#refusal-not-in-world), [`not_ready`](#refusal-not-ready), [`too_far`](#refusal-too-far), [`spawn_refused`](#refusal-spawn-refused), [`no_such_piece`](#refusal-no-such-piece)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `manifest` | string | at most 1024 characters | The showroom build's folder, or its manifest.json. Default (0.8.3): the XF Finish Showroom builds the game itself has staged (its archive/pc/mod folder), each with the manifest it ships inside the mod or, for an older build, this machine's build with the same bytes; every one is used, so a preset is found in whichever holds it. The answer's showroom_found names them. |
| `manifests` | array of string | 1 to 4 items; each at most 1024 characters | Several showroom builds' folders or manifests, to set out their presets together. |
| `presets` | array of string | 1 to 24 items; each at most 120 characters | Which presets, by name, preset ID or appearance, in lineup order. Default: all of them (at most 24). |
| `layout` | string | `arc`, `row` | arc (default): on a circle about the camera or V, each head facing it. row: a straight line across the view, all facing back along it. |
| `spacing_m` | number | 0.3 to 5 | Distance between neighbouring heads, 0.3 to 5 m. Default 0.7. |
| `distance_m` | number | 0.8 to 10 | How far each head's eyes are from the camera (or V's eyes), 0.8 to 10 m, in 3D. Default 2.5. |
| `height_m` | number | 0.5 to 3.2 | The heads' eye height above V's ground, 0.5 to 3.2 m. Default: the camera's height (anchor camera), else a head's natural 1.69 m. The pedestals reach 1.5 m below a head's natural place, so a head raised more than that ends in the air. |
| `lateral_m` | number | -5 to 5 | Shift the whole lineup to the right as the camera or V sees it (negative: left), -5 to 5 m. With distance_m equal to photo_frame's distance_m (the camera to V's face), a head at lateral 0.6 stands beside her on the same arc and appears at her scale. Default 0. |
| `anchor` | string | `camera`, `v` | camera (default in photo mode) or v (default in normal play). |
| `replace` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Remove the heads set out earlier first (default true). |
| `avoid_walls` | boolean | `true`, `false` | 0.7: check each head's eyes for free space and a clear sight line (world_probe) and move a blocked head back or sideways, saying so in moved_for_space. Default true. |

### `showroom_light`

**Light the finish showroom.** Spawns a light rig built from the game's own character-creator rig (native lumens, falloff, cones and shadows): rig creator (all 15 lights), creator_face (the 13 that reach the head, no shadows) or key (the key light alone). target each (default) gives every head its own rig in its own frame, so each gets the same light; piece lights one head; v lights V the same way, for the fidelity check. Rigs of neighbouring heads also light each other: the answer estimates by how much and warns above 5 %. Rigs stay put when heads turn, so a turn sweeps the highlights.

- **Command:** `showroom.light`, run by the tools (it may call the bridge several times)
- **Permission:** Set up the finish showroom (`write-showroom`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** showroom.clear with what: lights.
- **Refusals:** [`codeware_missing`](#refusal-codeware-missing), [`showroom_missing`](#refusal-showroom-missing), `showroom_manifest_missing`, `showroom_manifest_bad`, `showroom_not_staged`, [`not_in_world`](#refusal-not-in-world), [`not_ready`](#refusal-not-ready), [`too_far`](#refusal-too-far), `no_showroom`, [`no_such_piece`](#refusal-no-such-piece), [`spawn_refused`](#refusal-spawn-refused)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `manifest` | string | at most 1024 characters | The showroom build's folder, or its manifest.json (its rig entity is used). Default (0.8.3): the staged builds, found as showroom_spawn finds them (the first one's rig). |
| `rig` | string | `creator`, `creator_face`, `key`, `none` | creator (default), creator_face, key, or none (remove every rig and keep the heads, as showroom_clear with what: lights). |
| `target` | string | `each`, `piece`, `v` | each (default): a rig per head; piece: the head given by piece; v: V herself. |
| `piece` | integer | 0 to 23 | The head's index in the lineup (0 is the first), with target piece. |
| `replace` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Remove the rigs placed earlier first (default true). |

### `showroom_rotate`

**Turn the showroom heads.** Turns showroom heads on their pedestals: yaw_deg relative to how they were set out (0 faces the camera or V as at spawn, positive turns them to their left), delta_deg from where they are now, or a turntable sweep from from_deg to to_deg in steps (default -60 to 60 in 7 steps), waiting settle_ms at each and, with capture, taking a screenshot of region (default the whole window) at each step. Light rigs don't turn, so the highlights sweep across each face. After a sweep the heads go back where they were unless return is false.

- **Command:** `showroom.rotate`, run by the tools (it may call the bridge several times)
- **Permission:** Set up the finish showroom (`write-showroom`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** showroom.rotate with yaw_deg 0 faces them as set out; a result's undo turns them back exactly.
- **Refusals:** `no_showroom`, [`no_such_piece`](#refusal-no-such-piece), [`not_spawned_yet`](#refusal-not-spawned-yet), `capture_no_window`, `capture_minimized`, `capture_not_foreground`, `capture_blank`, `capture_failed`

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pieces` | array of integer | 1 to 24 items; each 0 to 23 | Which heads by lineup index (default all). |
| `yaw_deg` | number | -180 to 180 | Yaw relative to how the heads were set out, -180 to 180. |
| `delta_deg` | number | -180 to 180 | Turn by this much from where they are now, -180 to 180. |
| `sweep` | object | the fields below | A turntable sweep instead of one turn. |
| `sweep.from_deg` | number | -180 to 180 | First angle, relative to how the heads were set out. Default -60. |
| `sweep.to_deg` | number | -180 to 180 | Last angle. Default 60. |
| `sweep.steps` | integer | 1 to 36 | How many angles, 1 to 36, evenly spaced. Default 7. |
| `sweep.settle_ms` | integer | 0 to 5000 | Wait at each angle before the screenshot, 0 to 5000 ms. Default 400. |
| `sweep.capture` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Take a screenshot at each angle (default false). |
| `sweep.region` | string | `full`, `center-16x9`, `head-and-shoulders`, `face`, `eyes`, `full-body`, `cc-eyes` | The area each screenshot keeps (as capture_screenshot). Default: the whole window. |
| `sweep.name` | string | at most 60 characters; matches `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,60}$` | Short label for the screenshots' files. |
| `sweep.return` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Turn the heads back where they were afterwards (default true). |

### `showroom_clear`

**Clear the finish showroom.** Removes the showroom's heads (what: pieces), its light rigs (lights) or both (all, the default). The kill switch and loading a save do the same.

- **Command:** `showroom.clear`, the bridge method `showroom.clear`
- **Permission:** Set up the finish showroom (`write-showroom`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** showroom.spawn and showroom.light set them out again.

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `what` | string | `all`, `pieces`, `lights` | all (default), pieces or lights. |

### `showroom_state`

**Read the finish showroom.** Lists the showroom heads and light rigs the bridge spawned: their preset, place, yaw and whether they are in the world yet, and whether Codeware is loaded.

- **Command:** `showroom.state`, the bridge method `showroom.state`
- **Permission:** Look (`read`)
- **Changes the game:** No
- **Undo:** nothing to undo

No parameters.

## NPC direction

Spawn XF actors (never saved), pick NPCs near V, and direct them: walk, follow, turn, place, speak (voiced, text or a caller's subtitle), look, set a face, gesture, and offer V dialogue choices whose pick comes back as an event. Releasing, the kill switch, the pause, a handover or loading a save gives everything back.

### `npc_list`

**List the NPCs near V.** The NPCs within radius_m of V (default 15, at most 40): each one's id (for npc_pick), record, distance and place, whether it is part of the street crowd, whether it is protected (a quest character, a companion, a vendor, police, a child, a boss, or in a story scene) with the reasons, whether it is busy (sitting or leaning somewhere, fighting, hostile to V), whether npc_pick would take it (pickable: a plain passer-by of the street crowd, not busy), and which are the session's own. Changes nothing.

- **Command:** `npc.list`, the bridge method `npc.list`
- **Permission:** Look (`read`)
- **Changes the game:** No
- **Undo:** nothing to undo
- **Refusals:** [`not_in_world`](#refusal-not-in-world), [`codeware_missing`](#refusal-codeware-missing)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `radius_m` | number | 1 to 40 | How far from V to look, 1 to 40 metres. Default 15. |
| `max` | integer | 1 to 40 | At most this many, 1 to 40. Default 20. |

### `npc_pick`

**Pick an NPC near V.** Adopts one plain passer-by of the street crowd within 30 m of V (its id from npc_list, pickable) so the bridge can make it look at someone, change its face and say a line; it is never moved, placed, turned, given a gesture or a stance, or removed, and it keeps walking its own way. Anyone else is refused: protected NPCs (story characters, companions, vendors, police, children, bosses, anyone in a scene) and every NPC outside the street crowd (a quest may use one without marking it), and busy ones (sitting or leaning somewhere, fighting, hostile to V). A pick that becomes busy or protected later is given back at once (npc.auto_released), and its gaze, face and lines are taken back on its release, the kill switch, the pause and a handover; a load takes the NPC itself away. Answers the NPC's handle (p1, p2, ...). Changes nothing by itself.

- **Command:** `npc.pick`, the bridge method `npc.pick`
- **Permission:** Look (`read`)
- **Changes the game:** No
- **Undo:** nothing to undo
- **Refusals:** [`not_in_world`](#refusal-not-in-world), [`in_combat`](#refusal-in-combat), [`in_vehicle`](#refusal-in-vehicle), [`in_scene`](#refusal-in-scene), [`not_v`](#refusal-not-v), [`codeware_missing`](#refusal-codeware-missing), `npc_protected`, `npc_busy`, `npc_not_found`, [`too_far`](#refusal-too-far), `limit`

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` (required) | string | 1 to 64 characters | The NPC's id from npc_list. |

### `npc_status`

**Read the NPCs the bridge directs.** The session's actors and picked NPCs: each one's handle, cast or record, whether it has appeared, where it is, what it is doing (walking, following, turning), its lines still showing, its gaze, face and gesture; the dialogue choices showing, if any; and the limits (3 actors, 4 picks, 30 m). Changes nothing.

- **Command:** `npc.status`, the bridge method `npc.status`
- **Permission:** Look (`read`)
- **Changes the game:** No
- **Undo:** nothing to undo

No parameters.

### `npc_spawn`

**Bring in an XF actor.** Brings an XF actor into the world near V: cast is one of XF's own passers-by (a copy of an ordinary base-game civilian, never a story character), placed ahead_m metres along V's facing and side_m to her right (or at a world point), on walkable ground within 30 m of V, facing V (or face another NPC or face_point). out_of_sight lets the bridge choose a walkable spot V can't see (outside her view or behind a wall, min_m to max_m from her, 12 to 25 by default), so the actor walks in from somewhere rather than appearing; out_of_view waits until the spot isn't on screen. The masked casts cover the mouth with a mask or respirator, so lines without lip movement read naturally. By default the actor is friendly to V, can't be killed and has calm reactions; attitude neutral or hostile, immortal false and reactions game make a stand-in that can be shot (when a fight begins the bridge stops directing it and its own AI takes over, npc.handed_back; if it dies its body stays until released). It is never saved: npc_release, the kill switch or loading a save removes it, and game_save refuses while one is out. At most 3 at once. Answers its handle (a1, a2, a3) at once; npc.spawned follows in the event stream when it appears. Needs Codeware and the -writes package's actor records.

- **Command:** `npc.spawn`, the bridge method `npc.spawn`
- **Permission:** Direct NPCs (`write-npc`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** The result's undo releases the actor (npc_release with how despawn); the kill switch and loading a save remove it too.
- **Refusals:** [`not_in_world`](#refusal-not-in-world), [`in_combat`](#refusal-in-combat), [`in_vehicle`](#refusal-in-vehicle), [`in_scene`](#refusal-in-scene), [`not_v`](#refusal-not-v), `cast_unknown`, [`codeware_missing`](#refusal-codeware-missing), `record_missing`, [`not_ready`](#refusal-not-ready), [`not_streamed`](#refusal-not-streamed), `not_walkable`, [`spawn_refused`](#refusal-spawn-refused), [`too_far`](#refusal-too-far), `limit`, `no_hidden_spot`

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cast` (required) | string | `woman_corpo`, `man_corpo`, `woman_nightlife`, `man_youngster`, `woman_lowlife`, `man_lowlife`, `woman_masked`, `man_masked`, `research_crowd_record`, `research_npc_base` | Which actor: woman_corpo, man_corpo, woman_nightlife, man_youngster, woman_lowlife or man_lowlife; woman_masked or man_masked wear a mask or respirator over the mouth (for lines without lip movement); research_crowd_record and research_npc_base are for the session-9 comparison only. |
| `ahead_m` | number | -30 to 30 | Metres along V's facing (negative: behind her), -30 to 30. |
| `side_m` | number | -30 to 30 | Metres to V's right (negative: left), -30 to 30. Default 0. |
| `at_point` | array of number | exactly 3 items | A world point instead of ahead_m and side_m. |
| `face` | string | matches `^(v\|[ap][0-9]{1,5})$` | Face V ("v", the default) or another NPC (its handle). |
| `face_point` | array of number | exactly 3 items | Face this world point instead. |
| `appearance` | string | at most 96 characters; matches `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$` | One of the actor's appearances by name (default: the cast's own look, or random). |
| `variant` | integer | 0 to 31 | Which of the cast's own looks (npc_status lists them per cast), from 0. Default 0. |
| `out_of_view` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Appear only when the spot isn't on screen. |

| `min_m` | number | 3 to 30 | With out_of_sight: at least this far from V, 3 to 30 m. Default 12. |
| `max_m` | number | 3 to 30 | With out_of_sight: at most this far from V, 3 to 30 m. Default 25. |
